subject.title: [Feature] Telegram Inline Query Support (@botname in any chat)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in Telegram inline-query support inside the bundled Telegram plugin, and what authorization, cache, session, and execution defaults should it use?
rationale: The implementation owner is clear, but routing arbitrary-chat inline query text into agents changes a Telegram security boundary and needs maintainer-owned product/security defaults before automation can safely implement it.

options.title: Approve constrained opt-in inline mode
options.body: Add an explicit inline-query opt-in with account-level authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for user-specific results, bounded agent execution, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer behind Guest/Bot-to-Bot design
options.body: Keep this open until the broader arbitrary-chat Telegram ingress policy settles, then implement inline queries using the shared approved boundary.

options.title: Reject built-in inline mode for now
options.body: Decline bundled inline-query support and document separate Telegram bots or future plugin seams as the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained opt-in inline mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit inline-query opt-in with account-level authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for user-specific results, bounded agent execution, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue needs a Telegram plugin product/security boundary decision, and steipete has recent history across the Telegram handler/status/docs surfaces.
